Messages.Author: Jeroen du Chatinier
Messages.Body:
A quick question.

If I (for whatever reason) have two master phases, can I play two
OOT-masters (2 suddens, for example)?

In 1.6.2 it only says: "You may not play a second out-of-turn card
against the same master phase". But since I have a second master
phase, can I play my second OOT-master against that second (different)
master phase?

I think the answer is no, because you gain that second master phase
_during_ your masterphase, but an official ruling would be helpful.

Or maybe Ansons/RoG text is totally irrelevant, because an OOT-master
counts against your next master _phase_, and the above two cards give
you an additional master phase _action_.

Still, a ruling would clear things up.

Thanks in advance,

Jeroen du Chatinier

Messages.Author: Jozxyqk
Messages.Body:
Jeroen du Chatinier <jero...@hotmail.com> wrote:
> A quick question.

> If I (for whatever reason) have two master phases, can I play two
> OOT-masters (2 suddens, for example)?

> In 1.6.2 it only says: "You may not play a second out-of-turn card
> against the same master phase". But since I have a second master
> phase, can I play my second OOT-master against that second (different)
> master phase?

There is only ever one Master Phase per turn.
Anson,etc only give you extra Master Phase *Actions*.

Therefore there's currently no way in the game to play more than one
out-of-turn Master in the same 'round'.

Messages.Author: Frederick Scott
Messages.Body:
Jeroen du Chatinier wrote:
>
> A quick question.
>
> If I (for whatever reason) have two master phases, can I play two
> OOT-masters (2 suddens, for example)?
>
> In 1.6.2 it only says: "You may not play a second out-of-turn card
> against the same master phase". But since I have a second master
> phase, can I play my second OOT-master against that second (different)
> master phase?

In addition to the technical explaination for this that others have
contributed, I'll point something out for you:

Since people tend to think of using an OOT master at the penalty of
a master phase action in the next master phase, it's natural to assume
you're "borrowing" you next master phase action. Therefore, a lot of
people naturally make the leap that if you have two master phase actions
in the next turn, you ought to be able to borrow against both of them,
right? (Well, of course, a strict reading of the rules does not support
this, but aside from that...)

...except that you're assuming you'll even HAVE two master phases come
the next round. Anson can be torporize, The Parenthenon can be burnt
or stolen, Rumors of Gehenna can be voted off the island by the time
your next master phase rolls around. Such a reading of the rules fails
to address what happens if you've played two OOT masters and then lost
your extra master phase action come the time you're expected to pay for
them.

Fred

Messages.Author: Rafe
Messages.Body:
> ...except that you're assuming you'll even HAVE two master phases come
> the next round. Anson can be torporize, The Parenthenon can be burnt
> or stolen, Rumors of Gehenna can be voted off the island by the time
> your next master phase rolls around. Such a reading of the rules fails
> to address what happens if you've played two OOT masters and then lost
> your extra master phase action come the time you're expected to pay for
> them.

This is all hypothetical, since (as you point out) this isn't how the
OoT master rule being discussed works, but the above situation doesn't
always apply - there is a guaranteed way of getting an additional
master phase that cannot be lost before the next master phase, which
is by using Synesios' special:

Independent: Synesios has 2 votes. You may pay a pool when you play a
Master: Out-of-Turn card to gain an extra Master Phase Action in your
next master phase. Synesios cannot use cards that require Celerity.
Scarce.

Synesios' special takes effect once you pay for it, so even if he
burns before your next master phase you still get the extra MPA. So
the 'you can't play a OoT master against your extra MPA because you
might lose it if Anson/Rumors/Parthenon etc is burnt/stolen/etc'
argument wouldn't apply to that case.

But it doesn't really matter as the rules limit OoT masters to one
against each master phase anyway, as you say :-)

- Rafe
